newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA BACK ON COURSE WITH WIN OVER LUXEMBOURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA BACK ON COURSE WITH WIN OVER LUXEMBOURG.

text.p: Russia got their World Cup campaign back on track on Wednesday with a comfortable 3-0 win over Luxembourg in Moscow that will help erase memories of last month's 1-1 draw in Cyprus.
The Russians never got into top gear but were content to secure three points against a Luxembourg side reduced to 10 men for the final half hour.
Metz defender Jeff Strasser was sent off for dangerous play as he tried to prevent Igor Simutenkov making a pass inside the area that let Sergei Grishin in for Russia's second goal.
A minute later, Reggiana striker Simutenkov had a free header from a long through ball to make it 3-0. Valery Kechinov had scored the first after 20 minutes.

The result leaves Russia in second place in group five, with 11 points from five games. They are two points behind Israel, who beat Cyprus 2-0 at home on Wednesday, but the Israelis, who travel to Moscow on June 8, have played a game more.
